exposure: Women with type 1 diabetes were compared to women without diabetes.
cohort: 107 pregnancies to women with type 1 diabetes and 27,075 pregnancies to women without diabetes in Victoria, Australia, between 2010 and 2013
finding: Women with type 1 diabetes experienced adverse obstetric and neonatal outcomes, including higher rates of Cesarean delivery, preterm birth, and perinatal death, even when managed in a specialist setting.
mod_finding: Women with type 1 diabetes were more likely to have had labor induced (aOR, 3.0; 95% CI, 2.0-4.5) and a caesarean delivery (aOR, 4.6; 95% CI, 3.1-7.0).
gest_age: Median gestational age was shorter for babies of mothers with type 1 diabetes (37.3 weeks) compared to those without diabetes (39.4 weeks)
birth_weight: Babies of mothers with type 1 diabetes were more likely to be large for gestational age.
